hypothesis: Avoiding new NAS entries in a fixed scheduled FOMC-statement identification window might improve after-cost robustness, but may discard profitable opportunities.

rule.timestamp: Actual causal admission receipt time under the unchanged baseline; source/broker clock must first be reconciled.
rule.within_window: Exclude that new signal. No deferred entry, post-window resurrection, altered stop or existing-position action.
rule.outside_window: Unchanged baseline eligibility. No policy surprise, statement sentiment, price move or future information is an input.
rule.unavailable: Incomplete calendar, later receipt/version or naive clock means unavailable/review; never silently no-event.

references.title: Gurkaynak, Sack and Swanson (2004), Do Actions Speak Louder Than Words?
references.role: Primary intraday evidence that policy actions and statement information can move asset prices. Not evidence that an entry exclusion is profitable.

references.title: Wongswan (2005), The Response of Global Equity Indexes to U.S. Monetary Policy Announcements
references.role: Section 2.1 describes a 10-minute-before/20-minute-after monetary-surprise window. Its equity-response analysis also uses a wider window. Neither is a recommended trading exclusion.

references.title: Federal Reserve meeting calendars and information
references.role: Agency dates and links are metadata leads. A page retrieved today does not establish what this research system knew before a historical entry.

references.title: Federal Reserve January 28, 2026 statement release header
references.role: The header explicitly states 2:00 p.m. EST for this release. Do not generalize that clock to every historical event or infer a CFD broker offset.

readiness: Calendar vintage, complete coverage, clock/contract reconciliation and separate full evaluation freeze required. No ongoing collection; stopped by user.
limitations: No financial outcome, interception count or calendar-to-signal feature join was computed.
Separate press conferences/unscheduled events and already open positions remain outside this proposed new-entry gate.
CFD fee, margin, historical contract and clock assumptions remain estimates/unresolved. No futures relabelling.
A narrower entry universe may reduce net profit and opportunity capture; no benefit is assumed.
